messages:
laura-support: FYI ticket #C-97412 — enterprise customer reporting metering mismatch for Private/VPC deployment. Dashboard shows ~2.4M tokens for the day, audit logs only show ~1.8M. Customer says invoice will be off. Can we triage?

miguel-sre: assigning. first pass: did they upgrade the metering agent recently or apply an NTP change? clock skew has been a common source.

laura-support: customer says they patched the agent last week (v1.3.7 -> v1.3.9) but didn't change host time config. They mentioned a short network outage at 02:15 UTC where the agent lost connectivity to collector.

anika-eng-infra: pinging meter-agent-bot for recent agent health and buffered event stats for that customer id (cust-redwood-EX42).

meter-agent-bot: [automated] agent_id=ma-7f2a status=running last_heartbeat=1728999600 queued_events=0 disk_buffer_usage=0% last_restart=1728540000

miguel-sre: bot shows queued_events=0 now, but that doesn't indicate past overflow. Do we have agent local logs around 02:00-03:00 UTC? ask customer for /var/log/redwood/meter-agent.log snippet.

laura-support: asked and they uploaded a snippet:

```
2024-11-05T01:58:42Z INFO  meter-agent Starting agent v1.3.9
2024-11-05T02:14:59Z WARN  meter-agent Connection to collector lost: timeout
2024-11-05T02:15:00Z ERROR meter-agent Buffer overflow: dropped_events=4123 buffer_size=1048576
2024-11-05T02:15:30Z INFO  meter-agent Attempting reconnect to collector
2024-11-05T02:16:05Z INFO  meter-agent Reconnected, flushing 0 events (disk buffer exhausted)
2024-11-05T02:16:10Z INFO  meter-agent Clock adjust: -120s (NTP)
2024-11-05T02:16:11Z INFO  meter-agent Resumed event ingestion
```

miguel-sre: interesting — buffer overflow logged and then NTP adjusted clock back 2 minutes. If events were dropped, they won't show in audit log, but why does dashboard show MORE tokens (2.4M) than audit logs (1.8M)? That suggests duplicate counting or a replay from another path.

anika-eng-infra: two hypotheses: 1) agent dropped events on ingress (we see that) but another collector ingested duplicates during reconnect (old metrics replayed) causing inflated usage in BI pipeline; or 2) dashboard aggregates include both 'ingested' and 'reprocessed' markers — billing uses finalized meter (invoices) but audit logs are agent-level. Need to check pipeline logs around reconnect window and collector-side de-dup.

rachel-billing: pulled billing pipeline traces for cust-redwood-EX42 between 01:50-02:30 UTC. I see a spike in token counts on collector nodes col-03 and col-07 at 02:16:05 exactly when agent reported reconnect. There are repeated event IDs with different ingestion timestamps. Looks like dedupe failed for ~4300 events.

laura-support: so dropped vs duplicated — can you explain in plain terms for the customer? they want to understand whether invoiceable tokens are accurate.

rachel-billing: short: our billing pipeline normally deduplicates events using event_id + agent_id + monotonic counter. During the reconnect, agent restarted a local monotonic counter (v1.3.9 bug) which reset to zero after a crash. The collector treated those as new events (not duplicates) and committed them. The audit log shows what the agent wrote to disk (so it reflects the actual successful emissions), while the billing pipeline counts what the collector accepted. That mismatch explains higher dashboard/invoice numbers.

miguel-sre: recorded root cause: agent crash + buffer overflow + monotonic counter reset on restart + collector dedupe gap. Short-term mitigation: patch agent to v1.3.10 which includes monotonic counter persistence across restarts; also change collector dedupe window to consider agent restart flag.

anika-eng-infra: action items:
- eng-infra: deploy v1.3.10 to private agent channel and provide hotfix script to persist counter for existing installs. (owner: anika, ETA 48h)
- eng-sre: run collector reprocess job to drop duplicates for cust-redwood-EX42 between 02:15-02:20 UTC and recalc billing usage. (owner: miguel, ETA 24h)
- billing: hold invoice adjustments until reprocess completes; prepare provisional credit if pipeline confirms double-count. (owner: rachel-billing, ETA 36h)
- support: send interim status to customer explaining cause and next steps. (owner: laura-support, ETA 2h)

laura-support: draft message to customer: "We found the cause: a transient agent crash and buffer overflow caused the local monotonic counter to reset on restart, which led the collector to accept re-ingested events as distinct. We're reprocessing to remove duplicates and will adjust invoice if needed. Patch and hotfix are scheduled." OK?

miguel-sre: please include that they can optionally enable strict local persistence now with our hotfix to avoid future resets. Also mention that we observed a small clock adjustment (-120s) which can complicate ordering but is not the primary cause.

rachel-billing: running the reprocess now (job id rp-20241105-EX42). Preliminary estimate: ~4300 duplicate events -> ~520k tokens. If confirmed we'll issue a credit.

meter-agent-bot: [automated] reprocess_job_started job_id=rp-20241105-EX42 submitted_by=miguel-sre queued_at=1729001400

laura-support: sending update to customer now. I'll post final closure once billing confirms the credit. Thanks all :thumbsup:

miguel-sre: postmortem note for eng-docs: add a check in our metering health dashboard for "recent buffer overflow + restart" pattern and alert as high priority. That should catch these earlier.

anika-eng-infra: agreed. I'll open a ticket in infra backlog and add the hotfix artifact to private channel.

rachel-billing: update: reprocess complete at 1729001700. Duplicates removed, adjusted usage delta -525,312 tokens. Preparing credit memo.

laura-support: thanks — closing once customer acknowledges. Thread end."
